PHOTO: ALLEN EGENUSE J / The Hindu The ECI has introduced an additional declaration form along with Form 6 which require these voters to provide details of their earlier electoral roll entries or that of their parents or grandparents NEW DELHI The Election Commission of India (ECI) has raised a razor-thin justification to allegations that it has unauthorisedly amended Form 6 to introduce extra-statutory requirements for voters whose names were deleted in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to return to the electoral rolls. Use of Form 6 to re-enlist voters left out during SIR challenged in Supreme Court storyline 1 Supreme Court assures no deleted voters will be prosecuted for submitting Form 6 storyline 1 The wordplay in an ECI affidavit is about an additional declaration form provided alongside Form 6. The declaration form requires deleted voters to provide details of their earlier electoral roll entries or that of their parents or grandparents. The ECI calls the exercise ‘mapping’. Any perceived mismatch of lack of detail in this regard is broadly termed as ‘logical discrepancy’. In Delhi alone, there were initially 33.12 lakh cases of ‘no-mapping’ or ‘logical discrepancy’. CEC row LIVE updates https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/cec-row-sir-live-updates-supreme-court-hearing-gyanesh-kumar-oct-27-2026/article71629879.ece Petitioners have claimed in court that the additional declaration form was an illegal amendment to Form 6, and has become a tool for exclusion of voters. The ECI cannot have unilaterally altered Form 6. That was the job of the Centre, and not the ECI, they have contended. Declaration part of Form 6 changed since SIR in Bihar Declaration part of Form 6 changed since SIR in Bihar ECI officials say a separate declaration form with Form 6 and Form 8 was approved by the three-member commission when the SIR process began in Bihar last year and was ratified again in phases two and three Declaration part of Form 6 changed since SIR in Bihar storyline 1 The October 26 affidavit, displaying a united face among Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, argues that the petitioners have got it wrong. The affidavit maintained that Form 6 was never changed. The additional declaration form was not a part of the statutory Form 6. Also Read: SC says ‘will examine’ petitioners’ ‘innocuous’ plea to direct ECI to preserve or file in court ‘complete’ SIR records https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/sc-says-will-examine-petitioners-innocuous-plea-to-direct-eci-to-preserve-or-file-in-court-complete-sir-records/article71630549.ece “The additional declaration form is a document provided by SIR orders and is NOT a part of Form 6, which is the statutory Form for inclusion in the electoral roll,” the ECI underscored. The phrase “for inclusion in the electoral roll” used in the ECI affidavit does not fully explain the role of Form 6. Form 6 is meant exclusively to apply as a fresh voter. Petitioners have challenged this aspect too. They argue that pre-existing electors deleted during the SIR exercise are being forced to apply as fresh voters, compelled to do so under the threat of penal consequences. Changes to Form 6 not made by court; post-retirement immunity to CEC not given to even judges: Supreme Court Changes to Form 6 not made by court; post-retirement immunity to CEC not given to even judges: Supreme Court “A protection when in office is always understood. But the ‘was’ in the provision is perhaps only protection with regard to the President. It does not apply even to judges... Look at the Judges Inquiry Act,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi said Changes to Form 6 not made by court; post-retirement immunity to CEC not given to even judges: Supreme Court storyline 1 ECI said the additional declaration was part of an online push to assist voters. They could file their required details in a single document rather than produce multiple documents for verification like in the Bihar SIR. On September 26, the ECI had issued a press note that the “declaration attached to Form 6 has been upheld by the Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used”. But the Supreme Court had orally clarified on October 12, in open court, that it had neither approved nor disapproved the controversial alterations made to Form 6 in its May 27 judgment in the Bihar SIR challenge. EC reverts to allowing Form 6 submission without attached declaration in non-SIR States EC reverts to allowing Form 6 submission without attached declaration in non-SIR States While Form 6 is normally used for new voter registrations, during the SIR process, it was also used for re-enlisting those who had been deleted during the enumeration phase. A separate declaration had been added to the physical form regarding the mapping of self or parents with electoral rolls from the period of the previous SIR EC reverts to allowing Form 6 submission without attached declaration in non-SIR States storyline 1 The oral remark from the Bench had also clearly referred to the additional declaration form as part of the “new Form 6”. “When the Bihar SIR issue was heard and decided, the new Form 6 was not there. The new Form 6 was neither approved nor disapproved by us. But we will examine it now,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi, who is part of the Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, had observed orally. The remark had come in response to a petition filed by Priya Mishra against the Union government challenging the alterations made to Form 6 to register new voters during the SIR exercises undertaken across multiple States.
